This table contains information about the printers installed on Windows computers. It only stores printers installed for the computer as a whole, not printers installed for specific users, and pulls data from the Win32_Printer WMI class. More info on this class can be found here: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa394363%28v=VS.85%29.aspx

Name Type NULL Comment
◆printerID int ☐ PK
AssetID int ☐ ⇨ tblAssets.AssetIDFK
Capabilitydescriptions nvarchar ☒ Array of free-form strings that provide detailed explanations for the printer features indicated in the Capabilities array. Each entry of this array is related to an entry in the Capabilities array that is located in the same index.
Caption nvarchar ☒ Short description.
Comment nvarchar ☒ Comment for a print queue.
EnableBIDI bit ☒ If TRUE, the printer can print bidirectional.
Horizontalresolution numeric ☒ Horizontal resolution of the printer—in pixels per inch.
Local bit ☒ If TRUE, the printer is not attached to a network. If both the Local and Network properties are set to TRUE, then the printer is a network printer.
Location nvarchar ☒ Physical location of the printer.
Network bit ☒ If TRUE, the printer is a network printer. If both the Local and Network properties are set to TRUE, then the printer is a network printer.
Portname nvarchar ☒ Port that is used to transmit data to a printer. If a printer is connected to more than one port, the names of each port are separated by commas.
Printjobdatatype nvarchar ☒ Data type of a print job waiting for the Windows-based printing device.
Printprocessor nvarchar ☒ Name of the print spooler that handles print jobs.
Sharename nvarchar ☒ Share name of the Windows-based printing device. Example: \\PRINTSERVER1\PRINTER2
Status nvarchar ☒ Current status of the object. Various operational and nonoperational statuses can be defined. Operational statuses include: "OK", "Degraded", and "Pred Fail" (an element, such as a SMART-enabled hard disk drive, may be functioning properly but predicting a failure in the near future). Nonoperational statuses include: "Error", "Starting", "Stopping", and "Service". The latter, "Service", could apply during mirror-resilvering of a disk, reload of a user permissions list, or other administrative work. Not all such work is online, yet the managed element is neither "OK" nor in one of the other states.
verticalresolution numeric ☒ Vertical resolution, in pixels-per-inch, of the printer.
Lastchanged datetime ☐ Last time the table record was changed
DeviceID nvarchar ☒ Unique identifier of the printer on a system.

This table contains information about the processes that are running on a Windows computer. It only stores Windows computer data pulled from the Win32_Process WMI class. More info on this class can be found here: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa394372%28v=VS.85%29.aspx

Threadcount numeric ☒ Number of active threads in a process. An instruction is the basic unit of execution in a processor, and a thread is the object that executes an instruction. Each running process has at least one thread.
Priority numeric ☒ Scheduling priority of a process within an operating system. The higher the value, the higher priority a process receives. Priority values can range from 0 (zero), which is the lowest priority to 31, which is highest priority.

ProcessorId nvarchar ☒ Processor information that describes the processor features. For an x86 class CPU, the field format depends on the processor support of the CPUID instruction. If the instruction is supported, the property contains 2 (two) DWORD formatted values. The first is an offset of 08h-0Bh, which is the EAX value that a CPUID instruction returns with input EAX set to 1. The second is an offset of 0Ch-0Fh, which is the EDX value that the instruction returns. Only the first two bytes of the property are significant and contain the contents of the DX register at CPU reset—all others are set to 0 (zero), and the contents are in DWORD format.

⇧tblSerialnumber

This table stores the software serial numbers pulled from a Windows computer's registry. The registry locations Lansweeper searches for keys can be found in TsysSerials. Note that software serial numbers and software installations have nothing to do with each other. TblSerialnumber stores software serial numbers; tblSoftware(Uni) stores software installations. These tables cannot be linked. Software installation scanning recreates Add/Remove Programs, while software serial scanning searches the registry for serial numbers. It is perfectly possible for a serial to be left behind in the registry when the corresponding software package is uninstalled. If a serial is stored in tblSerialnumber, it was found in the computer's registry. Lansweeper isn’t saying that the corresponding software is installed on the machine. It is saying that it found the software serial in the computer's registry.

Name Type NULL Comment
◆SerialID int ☐ PK
AssetID int ☐ ⇨ tblAssets.AssetIDFK
Product nvarchar ☒ Name of the product
ProductID nvarchar ☒ ID of the product
ProductKey nvarchar ☒ Product key/software serial number/license key
Lastchanged datetime ☐ Last time the table record was changed

﻿

Communications provider type.

"RS232 Serial Port"

"Unspecified"

⇧tblSNMPAssetMac

This table stores the MAC addresses of the assets connected to your switch interfaces/ports. This data is pulled from SNMP on the switch. For each interface/port, Lansweeper stores the MAC address(es) of the last asset(s) to be detected on (connected to) that port. If a connected MAC pulled from SNMP matches the MAC address of a scanned asset, the Network Interfaces section of the switch page will link to the Lansweeper webpage of the connected asset. If the connected asset has not been scanned by Lansweeper, only the MAC address pulled from SNMP will be displayed on the switch page.

Lastchanged datetime ☐ Last time the table record was changed
Online bit ☐ Indicates whether or not the asset connected to the interface/port is online.
LastSeen datetime ☐ When the asset was detected on (connected to) the switch interface/port.

⇧tblSystemDrivers

This table contains information about the system drivers installed on a Windows computer. It stores Windows computer data pulled from the Win32_SystemDriver WMI class. More info on this class can be found here: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-systemdriver

Name Type NULL Comment
◆SystemDriverID bigint ☐ PK
AssetID int ☐ ⇨ tblAssets.AssetIDFK
SystemDriverUniID int ☐ ⇨ tblSystemDriversUni.SystemDriverUniIDFK
AcceptPause bit ☐ If TRUE, service can be paused.
AcceptStop bit ☐ If TRUE, service can be stopped.
DesktopInteract bit ☐ If TRUE, this service can create or communicate with windows on the desktop.
Started bit ☐ If TRUE, service has been started.
StartMode nvarchar ☐ Start mode of the system driver. Possible start modes are: Boot, System, Auto, Manual, Disabled. More info on these modes can be found in Microsoft’s WMI documentation.
StartName nvarchar ☒ Account name under which the service runs. Depending on the service type, the account name may be in the form of DomainName\Username. The service process will be logged using one of these two forms when it runs. If the account belongs to the built-in domain, .\Username can be specified. If NULL is specified, the service will be logged on as the LocalSystem account. For kernel or system-level drivers, StartName contains the driver object name (that is, \FileSystem\Rdr or \Driver\Xns) which the input and output (I/O) system uses to load the device driver. Additionally, if NULL is specified, the driver runs with a default object name created by the I/O system based on the service name. Example: "DWDOM\Admin".
State nvarchar ☒ Current state of the base service. Possible states are: Stopped, Start Pending, Stop Pending, Running, Continue Pending, Pause Pending, Paused, Unknown.
Status nvarchar ☒ Current status of the object. Various operational and nonoperational statuses can be defined. Operational statuses include: "OK", "Degraded" and "Pred Fail”. (An element, such as a SMART-enabled hard disk drive, may be functioning properly but predicting a failure in the near future.) Nonoperational statuses include: "Error", "Starting", "Stopping" and "Service". The latter, "Service", could apply during mirror-resilvering of a disk, reload of a user permissions list, or other administrative work. Not all such work is online, yet the managed element is neither "OK" nor in one of the other states.
PathName nvarchar ☒ Fully qualified path to the service binary file that implements the service. Example: "\SystemRoot\System32\drivers\afd.sys".
ErrorControl nvarchar ☒ Severity of the error if this service fails to start during startup. This value indicates the action taken by the startup program if failure occurs. All errors are logged by the computer system. Possible ErrorControl values are: Ignore, Normal, Severe, Critical, Unknown. More info on these values can be found in Microsoft’s WMI documentation.
ServiceType nvarchar ☒ Type of service provided to calling processes.
ExitCode bigint ☒ Windows error code defining any problems encountered in starting or stopping the service. This property is set to ERROR_SERVICE_SPECIFIC_ERROR (1066) when the error is unique to the specific service, and information about the error is available in the ServiceSpecificExitCode property. The service sets this value to NO_ERROR when running, and again upon normal termination.
ServiceSpecificExitCode bigint ☒ Service-specific error code for errors that occur while the service is either starting or stopping. The exit codes are defined by the service. This value is only set when the ExitCode property value is ERROR_SERVICE_SPECIFIC_ERROR (1066).
TagId bigint ☒ Unique tag value for this service in the group. A value of 0 (zero) indicates that the service has not been assigned a tag. A tag can be used for ordering service startup within a load order group.
LastChanged datetime ☐ Last time the table record was changed.

﻿

This table contains information about a tape drive on a computer system running Windows. It only stores Windows computer data pulled from the Win32_TapeDrive WMI class. More info on this class can be found here: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa394491%28v=VS.85%29.aspx

Name Type NULL Comment
◆Win32_TapeDriveid int ☐ PK
AssetID int ☐ ⇨ tblAssets.AssetIDFK
Availability numeric ☒
Availability and status of the device.
Value Meaning
1 (0x1) Other
2 (0x2) Unknown
3 (0x3) Running or Full Power
4 (0x4) Warning
5 (0x5) In Test
6 (0x6) Not Applicable
7 (0x7) Power Off
8 (0x8) Off Line
9 (0x9) Off Duty
10 (0xA) Degraded
11 (0xB) Not Installed
12 (0xC) Install Error
13 (0xD) Power Save - Unknown
The device is known to be in a power save mode, but its exact status is unknown.
14 (0xE) Power Save - Low Power Mode
The device is in a power save state but still functioning, and may exhibit degraded performance.
15 (0xF) Power Save - Standby
The device is not functioning, but could be brought to full power quickly.
16 (0x10) Power Cycle
17 (0x11) Power Save - Warning
The device is in a warning state, though also in a power save mode.
Capabilities nvarchar ☒
Array of capabilities of the media access device. For example, the device may support Random Access, removable media and Automatic Cleaning. In this case, the values 3, 7, and 9 would be written to the array.
Value Meaning
0 Unknown
1 Other
2 Sequential Access
3 Random Access
4 Supports Writing
5 Encryption
6 Compression
7 Supports Removable Media
8 Manual Cleaning
9 Automatic Cleaning
10 SMART Notification
11 Supports Dual-Sided Media
12 Predismount Eject Not Required
Caption nvarchar ☒ Short description of the object.
Compression numeric ☒ If TRUE, hardware data compression is enabled.
DefaultBlockSize numeric ☒ Default block size, in bytes, for this device.
Manufacturer nvarchar ☒ Manufacturer of the tape drive.
MaxBlockSize numeric ☒ Maximum block size, in bytes, for media accessed by this device.

⇧tblUsers

This table contains information about a user account on a computer system running Windows. It only stores Windows computer data pulled from the Win32_UserAccount WMI class. More info on this class can be found here: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa394507%28v=VS.85%29.aspx

Name Type NULL Comment
◆UserID int ☐ PK
AssetID int ☒ ⇨ tblAssets.AssetIDFK
Accounttype numeric ☒
Flags that describe the characteristics of a Windows user account.
Value (Dec/Hex) Meaning
256 (0x100) UF_TEMP_DUPLICATE_ACCOUNT
Local user account for users who have a primary account in another domain. This account provides user access to this domain only—not to any domain that trusts this domain.
512 (0x200) UF_NORMAL_ACCOUNT
Default account type that represents a typical user.
2048 (0x800) UF_INTERDOMAIN_TRUST_ACCOUNT
Account for a system domain that trusts other domains.
4096 (0x1000) UF_WORKSTATION_TRUST_ACCOUNT
Computer account for a computer system running Windows that is a member of this domain.
8192 (0x2000) UF_SERVER_TRUST_ACCOUNT
Account for a system backup domain controller that is a member of this domain.
Disabled bit ☒ If true then this user is disabled.
Fullname nvarchar ☒ The full name of the user.
Lockout bit ☒ If true, the user account is locked out of the Windows operating system.
Name nvarchar ☒ Name of the Windows user account on the domain that the Domain property of this class specifies.
PasswordChangeable bit ☒ If true the password of the user can be changed.
PasswordExpires bit ☒ If true, the password on this user account expires.
PasswordRequired bit ☒ If true then a password is required for this user.
SID nvarchar ☒ Security identifier (SID) for this account. A SID is a string value of variable length that is used to identify a trustee. Each account has a unique SID that an authority, such as a Windows domain, issues. The SID is stored in the security database. When a user logs on, the system retrieves the user SID from the database, places the SID in the user access token, and then uses the SID in the user access token to identify the user in all subsequent interactions with Windows security. Each SID is a unique identifier for a user or group, and a different user or group cannot have the same SID.
Status nvarchar ☒
Current status of an object. Various operational and nonoperational statuses can be defined. Operational statuses include: "OK", "Degraded", and "Pred Fail", which is an element such as a SMART-enabled hard disk drive that may be functioning properly, but predicts a failure in the near future. Nonoperational statuses include: "Error", "Starting", "Stopping", and "Service", which can apply during mirror resilvering of a disk, reloading a user permissions list, or other administrative work.
The values are:
"OK"
"Error"
"Degraded"
"Unknown"
"Pred Fail"
"Starting"
"Stopping"
"Service"
"Stressed"
"NonRecover"
"No Contact"
"Lost Comm"
Lastchanged datetime ☐ Last time the table record was changed
BuildInAdmin bit ☐ If true then this user is a built-in admin.

⇧tblVmwareDatastoreClusters

This table stores the datastore cluster information for VMware vCenter.

Name Type NULL Comment
◆DatastoreClusterID int ☐ PK
DatacenterID int ☐ ⇨ tblVmwareDatacenters.DatacenterIDFK
InternalKey nvarchar ☒ Datastore cluster internal key.
Name nvarchar ☐ The name of the datastore cluster.
FreeSpace bigint ☐ Total free space on this datastore cluster, in bytes. This value is the sum of the free space on all datastores that are part of this datastore cluster, and is updated periodically by the server.
Capacity bigint ☐ Total capacity of this datastore cluster, in bytes. This value is the sum of the capacity of all datastores that are part of this datastore cluster, and is updated periodically by the server.
DrsEnabled bit ☒ Indicates whether or not storage DRS is enabled.
IoLoadBalanceEnabled bit ☒ Indicates whether or not storage DRS takes into account storage I/O workload when making load balancing and initial placement recommendations.
DefaultIntraVmAffinity bit ☒ Specifies whether or not each virtual guest machine in this datastore cluster should have its virtual disks on the same datastore by default. If set to true, virtual guest machines will have all their virtual disks on the same datastore. If set to false, the virtual disks of a virtual guest machine may or may not be placed on the same datastore. If not set, the default value is true.
DefaultVmBehaviour nvarchar ☒ Specifies the default VMware DRS behavior for guests. This default behavior can be overridden on a per virtual machine basis.
LoadBalanceInterval int ☒ Specify the interval that storage DRS runs to load balance among datastores within a datastore cluster, in minutes. The default value is 480 minutes (= 8 hours).
SpaceUtilizationThreshold int ☒ Storage DRS makes storage migration recommendations if space utilization on one (or more) of the datastores is higher than the specified threshold. The default value is 80%.
MinSpaceUtilizationDifference int ☒ Storage DRS considers making storage migration recommendations if the difference in space utilization between the source and destination datastores is higher than the specified threshold. The default value is 5%.
IoLatencyThreshold int ☒ Storage DRS makes storage migration recommendations if I/O latency on one (or more) of the datastores is higher than the specified threshold, in millisecond. The default value is 15.
IoLoadImbalanceThreshold int ☒ Storage DRS makes storage migration recommendations if I/O load imbalance level is higher than the specified threshold, a number as value. The default value is 5.

⇧tblVmwareDatastoreClusterVmOverrides

Name Type NULL Comment
◆VmOverrideID int ☐ PK
DatastoreClusterID int ☐ The ID of the datastore cluster that this virtual machine override belongs to.
Enabled bit ☒ Indicates whether or not VirtualCenter is allowed to perform any storage migration or initial placement recommendations for this virtual guest machine on the pod datastore cluster. If this flag is false, the virtual guest machine is effectively excluded from storage DRS. The default value is true.
Behaviour nvarchar ☒ Specifies the particular storage DRS behavior for this virtual guest machine. Possible results are: automated and manual.
IntraVmAffinity bit ☒ Specifies whether or not to have the affinity rule for the virtual disks of this virtual guest machine. If not set, the default value is derived from the datastore cluster default DefaultIntraVmAffinity in tblVmwareDatastoreClusters.
IntraVmAntiAffinity nvarchar ☒ Specifies the disks for this virtual guest machine that should be placed on different datastores. A virtual guest machine cannot have both an affinity and an anti-affinity rule at the same time. Virtual guest machine disks that are not in this rule are unconstrained and can be placed either on the same datastore or on a different datastore as other disks from this virtual guest machine.

numCpuPkgs int ☒ Number of physical CPU packages on the ESX(i) host. Physical CPU packages are chips that contain one or more processors. Processors contained by a package are also known as CPU cores. For example, one dual-core package is comprised of one chip that contains two CPU cores.
numCpuThreads int ☒ Number of physical CPU threads on the ESX(i) host.
HostName nvarchar ☒ The host name of the ESX(i) host.
InternalKey nvarchar ☒ The VMware ESX(i) host key reference. Internal use only.
DatacenterID int ☒ The ID of the datacenter that the ESX(i) host belongs to, if any.
EsxiClusterID int ☒ The ID of the ESX(i) host cluster that the ESX(i) host belongs to, if any.
AdminDisabled bit ☒ If the flag is true, the permissions on the ESX(i) host have been modified such that it is only accessible through local console or an authorized centralized management application. This is supported in VirtualCenter only. Deprecated.
DnsAddresses nvarchar ☒ Comma-separated DNS addresses list of the ESX(i) host.
DefaultGateway nvarchar ☒ Comma-separated list containing the descriptions of the CPU packages.
DomainName nvarchar ☒ Domain of the ESX(i) host.
Dhcp bit ☒ Indicates whether client side DHCP is enabled on the ESX(i) host.
ConnectionState nvarchar ☒ The ESX(i) host connection state. Possible results are: connected, disconnected and notResponding.
PowerState nvarchar ☒ The ESX(i) host power state. Possible results are: poweredOff, poweredOn, standBy and unknown.
BootTime datetime ☒ The time when the ESX(i) host was booted.
UpTime bigint ☒ The time that the ESX(i) host is powered on, in seconds.
HostMaxVirtualDiskCapacity bigint ☒ The maximum theoretical virtual disk capacity supported by this ESX(i) host. Since API 5.5.
IpAddress nvarchar ☒ The IP address of the ESX(i) host.
Port int ☒ The port number.
SslThumbprint nvarchar ☒ The SSL thumbprint of the ESX(i) host, if known.
ManagementServerIp nvarchar ☒ IP address of the VirtualCenter server managing this ESX(i) host, if any.
Vendor nvarchar ☒ The hardware vendor identification.
Model nvarchar ☒ The system model identification.
Uuid nvarchar ☒ The hardware BIOS identification.
MemorySize bigint ☒ The physical memory size, in bytes.
CpuModel nvarchar ☒ The CPU model.
CpuMhz int ☒ The speed of the CPU cores. This is an average value if there are multiple speeds. The product of cpuMhz and numCpuCores is approximately equal to the sum of the MHz for all the individual cores on the ESX(i) host.

HTActive bit ☒ Indicates whether Hyper Threading is active.
HTAvailable bit ☒ Indicates whether Hyper Threading is available.
NumCpu int ☒ The number of CPUs.

⇧tblVolume

This table contains information about the area of storage on a hard disk. The data returned is for local volumes that are formatted, unformatted, mounted or offline. It only stores Windows computer data pulled from the Win32_Volume WMI class. More information about this class can be found on the following MSDN page https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa394515

Name Type NULL Comment
◆Volumeid int ☐ PK
AssetID int ☐ ⇨ tblAssets.AssetIDFK
Automount bit ☒ Indicates whether or not the volume is mounted to the file system automatically when the first I/O is issued. True = Volume automatically mounted with the issue of the first I/O | False = Volume will only be mounted by using the 'Mount' method or adding a drive letter or mount point.
BlockSize numeric ☒ Size in bytes of the block in the storage extent. If there is a variable block size, then the maximum block size in bytes is specified. If the block size is unknown or if a block concept is not valid
Capacity numeric ☒ Size of the volume in bytes.
Compressed bit ☒ Indicates whether or not the volume exists as one compressed entity. If file-based compression is supported, such as the NTFS file system, then the field is set to false. True = The volume exists as one compressed entity, such as a DoubleSpace volume | False = The volume does not exist as one compressed entity.
DeviceID nvarchar ☒ Unique identifier for the volume on this system..
DirtyBitSet bit ☒ Indicates whether or not the Chkdsk method is automatically run by the system at the next restart. True = Chkdsk is automatically run at the next restart | False = Chkdsk is not automatically run at the next restart.
DriveLetter nvarchar ☒ Drive letter assigned to a volume. This property is NULL for volumes without drive letters.
DriveType numeric ☒ Numeric value that corresponds to the type of disk drive that this logical disk represents. 0 = Unknown | 1 = No Root Directory | 2 = Removable Disk | 3 = Local Disk | 4 = Network Drive | 5 = Compact Disk | 6 = RAM Disk.
ErrorCleared bit ☒ Indicates whether or not the error given back in LastErrorCode is cleared. True = Error is cleared | False = Error is not cleared
ErrorDescription nvarchar ☒ Gives back additional information about the error given back in LastErrorCode.
ErrorMethodology nvarchar ☒ Type of error detection and correction supported by this storage extent.
FileSystem nvarchar ☒ File system on the logical disk.
FreeSpace numeric ☒ Space, in bytes, available on the logical disk.
IndexingEnabled bit ☒ Indicates whether or not context indexing is enabled. True = Context indexing is enabled | False = Context indexing is not enabled.
Label nvarchar ☒ Volume name of the logical disk. This property is null for volumes without a label. For FAT and FAT32 systems, the maximum length is 11 characters. For NTFS file systems, the maximum length is 32 characters.
Name nvarchar ☒ Label by which the object is known.
PageFilePresent bit ☒ Indicates whether or not the page file is present on the volume. True = Page file is present | False = Page file is not present.
SupportsDiskQuotas bit ☒ Indicates whether disk quotas are supported. 0 = False | 1 = True.
SupportsFileBasedCompression bit ☒ Indicates whether file compression is supported. 0 = False | 1 = True.
Lastchanged datetime ☐ Last time the table record was changed

﻿

⇧tblWinSAT

This table stores information found in the Windows System Assessment Tool (WinSAT). This tool can be found in a Windows computer's Control Panel, under Performance Information & Tools, and measures the computer's processor, memory, 2D graphics, 3D graphics and primary hard disk performance. An overall score, called the Windows Experience Index (WEI) score is then calculated. WinSAT data is pulled from the Win32_WinSAT WMI class. More info on this class can be found here: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa969204%28v=vs.85%29.aspx

Name Type NULL Comment
◆WinSatId int ☐ PK
AssetId int ☐ ⇨ tblAssets.AssetIDFK
CPUScore decimal ☒ A score for the processors on the computer.
D3DScore decimal ☒ A score for the three-dimensional graphics (gaming) capabilities of the computer.
DiskScore decimal ☒ A score for the sequential read throughput on the primary hard disk on the computer.
GraphicsScore decimal ☒ A score for the graphics capabilities of the computer.
MemoryScore decimal ☒ A score for the memory throughput and capacity of the computer.
WinSPRLevel decimal ☒ Base score for the computer.
WinSATAssessmentState tinyint ☒ State of the assessment. Value Meaning | 0 State Unknown | 1 Valid | 2 Incoherent With Hardware | 3 No Assessment Available | 4 Invalid |
LastChanged datetime ☐ Last time the table record was changed
